summary: Feed s113_double is degraded: 78.3% encrypted traffic exceeds IDS 60% tolerance and 8.3% of frames are sliced to 256 bytes, preventing full-payload inspection required by this IDS.

findings.root_cause: 78.3% of bytes are encrypted (TLS/HTTPS) vs 60% IDS tolerance. Traffic is forwarded through packet broker without SSL decryption/visibility, so IDS sees only encrypted payloads.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS cannot perform signature and anomaly detection on encrypted payloads; detection coverage drops sharply and encrypted attacks/malware will be missed.

recommended_fix.why: IDS needs cleartext payload for detection. Decrypt relevant TLS flows via dedicated SSL visibility appliance or broker decryption feature before forwarding to IDS, or filter to only decryptable/policy-required traffic to stay under 60% encrypted share.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is slicing packets to 256 bytes snaplen (143/1728 frames = 8.3% truncated, threshold 5%). Likely configured to save bandwidth/tool capacity, but this IDS requires full payload.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs full payload for signature matching and reassembly. Sliced frames lose application payload, causing missed exploits, incomplete flows, and false negatives.

recommended_fix.why: Disable slicing/truncation on the broker port feeding this IDS and forward full 1518-byte frames so IDS receives complete L7 payload for inspection.
